chunks: Abu Talib, may Allah have mercy on him, performed the 'aqiqah for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم on the seventh day, then he invited the family of Abu Talib, and they said, “What is this?” So he said:
They said, “For what reason did you name him Ahmad?” He said, “I named him Ahmad because of the praise of the people of the heaven and the earth for him.”

key_terms.أَحْمَدَ: a name of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم meaning the most praised or most praiseworthy
key_terms.عَقِيقَةُ: the 'aqiqah offered on behalf of a child
key_terms.عَقَّ: performed the 'aqiqah sacrifice for a newborn
key_terms.ٱلْأَرْضِ: the earth, meaning its inhabitants here

ai.seo_question: Why was the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم named Ahmad in this narration?
ai.summary: This report describes that Abu Talib performed the 'aqiqah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم on the seventh day after his birth and referred to him by the name Ahmad. It also gives a reason for this naming: that he would be praised by the inhabitants of the heaven and the earth. The narration reflects both an early family event and the distinguished status of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
